name: NCBI Bookshelf - Purves, Neuroscience, 2nd ed (2001)
what: Canonical 2nd-edition neuroscience textbook on NCBI Bookshelf (496 chapter/section records, NBK10799) covering molecular, cellular, systems and behavioral neurobiology - the biological ground truth for interpreting soma/neurite morphology and neurite-outgrowth phenotypes.
why_better: Old plan had no offline literature grounding for NTI interpretation (only a hand-tuned 'bio prior'); a canonical, citation-stable reference lets the app explain WHY a neurite-length or branch-angle change is biologically meaningful with a real section anchor, replacing the opaque prior with grounded, offline text.
evidence: 496 Bookshelf records under neurosci[book] (NCBI E-utilities esearch, Count=496); free to view at ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK10799
source_title: Neuroscience, 2nd edition (Purves D, Augustine GJ, Fitzpatrick D, et al.; Sinauer, 2001) - NCBI Bookshelf
license: unknown - freely available on NCBI Bookshelf but no explicit CC/open-redistribution license confirmed in this session (Bookshelf pages returned a reCAPTCHA challenge); verify redistribution rights before bundling full text
fit_small_data: high - single canonical textbook (~496 sections), small and directly on-topic, easy to chunk and index
fit_onnx_cpu: high - static text corpus; retrieval (embeddings + BM25) is CPU-bound and trivial; no model training involved
risk: Full-text redistribution rights unconfirmed; 2001 edition may predate some current PC12/DNT literature - pair with newer OA sources

name: NCBI Bookshelf - Siegel, Basic Neurochemistry, 6th ed (1999)
what: 6th-edition neurochemistry reference on NCBI Bookshelf (1,442 records, NBK20385) on molecular/cellular/medical neurochemistry - the mechanistic substrate for oxidative-stress (H2O2) and drug (doxorubicin) neurotoxicity and curcumin antioxidant biology.
why_better: Old plan's bio prior was a black box; a neurochemistry reference gives section-level mechanistic grounding for WHY H2O2/DOX/curcumin perturb the specific neuronal processes the four NTI sub-scores track (redox, apoptosis, neurite dynamics).
evidence: 1,442 Bookshelf records under bnchm[book] (NCBI E-utilities esearch, Count=1442); free at ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK20385
source_title: Basic Neurochemistry: Molecular, Cellular and Medical Aspects, 6th ed (Siegel GJ, Agranoff BW, Albers RW, et al.; Lippincott-Raven, 1999) - NCBI Bookshelf
license: unknown - free on NCBI Bookshelf; open-redistribution license unconfirmed in-session
fit_small_data: high - single reference, ~1,440 records, strongly on-mechanism for the toxin set
fit_onnx_cpu: high - static text; CPU retrieval only
risk: 1999 content (older); redistribution rights unconfirmed; larger chapter set to curate than a single textbook

name: NCBI Bookshelf - Methods of Behavior Analysis in Neuroscience, 2nd ed (2009)
what: Buccafusco-edited behavioral-methods reference on NCBI Bookshelf (NBK5228; 40+ specialist contributions) linking cellular morphology to functional readouts - useful for contextualizing PC12/SH-SY5Y assay endpoints and what 'neurite outgrowth' means functionally.
why_better: Old plan extracted 4 morphological parameters with no functional framing; this source lets the RAG layer map morphological NTI changes to behavioral/functional concepts, strengthening interpretability beyond a bare numeric index.
evidence: Book record confirmed via NCBI E-utilities esummary (uid 1411852, NBK5228, 'more than 40 field specialists'); free on Bookshelf
source_title: Methods of Behavior Analysis in Neuroscience, 2nd ed (Buccafusco JJ, ed.; CRC Press/Taylor & Francis, 2009) - NCBI Bookshelf
license: unknown - free on NCBI Bookshelf; open-redistribution license unconfirmed in-session
fit_small_data: high - bounded reference, on-topic for assay interpretation
fit_onnx_cpu: high - static text; CPU retrieval only
risk: Lower direct relevance to neurotoxicity than the two texts above; redistribution rights unconfirmed

name: NCBI Bookshelf - StatPearls (neurology/neurotoxicology subset)
what: Continuously-updated point-of-care monographs on Bookshelf; ~117,142 StatPearls records indexed in the Bookshelf database, including dedicated neurotoxicity and developmental-neurotoxicity entries - short, citable, clinical-grade definitions for NTI terms.
why_better: Old plan had no definitional/citation layer; StatPearls gives short, structured, peer-reviewed definitions the RAG can cite to explain NTI components in plain, clinically-accurate language offline, with stable per-chapter citations.
evidence: 117,142 'StatPearls' records in NCBI Bookshelf DB (NCBI E-utilities translation-stack Count=117,142); neurotoxicity entries present
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (StatPearls/Bookshelf terms; unverified in-session - Bookshelf pages reCAPTCHA-blocked) -> non-commercial + no-derivatives: reference-only, NOT shippable for redistribution

fit_onnx_cpu: high - static short docs; CPU retrieval only

name: Commercial neurotoxicology reference monographs (Tilson 'Handbook of Neurotoxicology'; Casarett & Doull's; Target Organ series)
what: The paywalled neurotoxicology/DNT canon: Tilson et al. 'Handbook of Neurotoxicology' (Humana Press/Springer, 2002, incl. chapter 'Risk Assessment of Developmental Neurotoxicants'), 'Casarett & Doull's Toxicology' (editions confirmed via publisher reviews), and Target Organ-series neurotoxicology volumes.
why_better: These are the authoritative DNT risk-assessment and mechanisms texts the old plan referenced only as a hand-coded prior; they supply the weight-of-evidence structure (DNT endpoints, life-stage sensitivity) that a knowledge-grounded NTI explanation should cite - but as reference, not shippable text.
evidence: Tilson ch. DOI 10.1007/978-1-59259-165-7_4 ('Handbook of Neurotoxicology', 2002) confirmed via Crossref; Casarett & Doull's 2nd/3rd-ed reviews confirmed via Crossref; exact 4th-ed chapter count and 'Principles of Neurotoxicology' Springer title NOT confirmed in this session (unverified)

name: OECD test & guidance documents (TG 426, TG 443 [correction], GD 377 DNT IVB neurite outgrowth)
what: OECD regulatory corpus for the neurotoxicity program: TG 426 (in vitro gene mutation / HGPRT), and the DNT IVB in vitro neurite-outgrowth guidance GD 377 (PC12-based). NOTE: the brief's 'TG 443' is the Extended One-Generation Reproductive Toxicity Study (EOGRTS), NOT a neurotest - flag this correction to the team.
why_better: Old plan applied a 'post-hoc bio prior' without an explicit regulatory test framework; ingesting OECD GD 377 / TG 426 gives the app an authoritative, free, redistributable source for what the PC12 neurite-outgrowth readout is supposed to measure and how results are interpreted, grounding the NTI in accepted assay semantics.
evidence: 17 Europe PMC records citing 'OECD Test No. 426'; TG 443 = 'Extended One Generation Reproductive Toxicity Study (EOGRTS)' confirmed via Beekhuijzen 2024 (DOI 10.1016/j.yrtph.2024.105665); GD 377 = DNT IVB neurite-outgrowth (OECD DNT framework). iLibrary PDF pages returned HTTP 403 in-session, so per-document page counts unverified
license: OECD standard (documents freely downloadable/redistributable; no CC) - shippable in an offline app
fit_small_data: high - a small, finite set of guidance documents; curate the DNT/neuro subset
fit_onnx_cpu: high - static guidance text; CPU retrieval only
risk: iLibrary PDFs were 403/bot-blocked in-session; the DNT IVB guidance number (GD 377) and its PC12 basis should be re-verified against a working iLibrary session before citing

name: EFSA DNT scientific opinions + 2025 in vivo DNT study database
what: EFSA's open scientific opinions on developmental neurotoxicity (e.g. the 2013 DNT potential opinion) plus a 2025 curated in vivo DNT study-results database - the EU regulatory-interpretation layer for DNT readouts.
why_better: Old plan had no regulatory-interpretation corpus; EFSA's open opinions and curated DNT study database let the RAG cite exactly how an authoritative body interprets neurodevelopmental endpoints, making the NTI's dose/time-response claims defensible and externally checkable.
evidence: 2013 EFSA DNT opinion (DOI 10.2903/j.efsa.2013.3471) and 2025 EFSA in vivo DNT database (DOI 10.1080/10408444.2025.2521280) both surfaced in search; EFSA opinions published open/CC BY
license: CC BY (EFSA open) - shippable in an offline app
fit_small_data: high - bounded set of opinions + one curated database; directly on DNT
fit_onnx_cpu: high - static text + structured study records; CPU retrieval only
risk: Wiley-hosted EFSA PDF URL failed DNS in-session; confirm exact downloadable format and CC-BY attribution string before bundling

name: ToxCast/Tox21 DNT NAM battery (Hall et al. 2026, Neurotoxicology)
what: The US EPA/NIEHS open-access in vitro DNT 'key neurodevelopmental process' (KNDP) battery: 95 chemicals screened across proliferation, apoptosis, cell migration, neuronal differentiation, neurite outgrowth, neuronal maturation, synaptogenesis, oligodendrocyte differentiation and network formation, plus zebrafish neurobehavior - with a benchmark-concentration / Pareto / ToxPi integration pipeline.
why_better: Old plan computed NTI in isolation with no high-throughput anchor; this open dataset lets the app compare its PC12 neurite-outgrowth readout against a 95-chemical, 9-endpoint DNT battery and cite the exact KNDP taxonomy, turning a single-assay index into a contextually calibrated one.
evidence: 95 chemicals; 9 KNDP in vitro endpoints + zebrafish neurobehavior (stated in abstract); Neurite outgrowth + fungicides showed highest % selective hits; OA in PMC13552535, Neurotoxicology 115:103485 (2026)
license: Open access (PMC) - shippable; verify exact article license (OA, likely CC) at ingest
fit_small_data: medium - 95 chemicals x 9 endpoints is a small, curatable data + text set; maps 1:1 to the neurite-outgrowth assay
fit_onnx_cpu: high - small structured data + OA text; CPU ingestion/retrieval only
risk: Broader historical ToxCast scale figures (e.g. 2,860 assays / 648 chemicals) could NOT be confirmed in-session and are NOT asserted here; the 2026 NAM-battery specifics are what is verified

name: Europe PMC / PMC OA subset (with commercial vs non-commercial license split)
what: The largest open biomedical full-text corpus (48,938,549 indexed records on Europe PMC; 12,296,246 with PMC full text; 8,273,746 open-access) - the raw pool to curate the neurotoxicity slice (e.g. 258,530 'neurotoxicity' PMC records; 27,685 'curcumin + neuroprotection').
why_better: Old plan had zero literature retrieval; Europe PMC's LICENSE: facets make it possible to separate the commercially-redistributable OA slice from the non-commercial slice, so the offline app can legally bundle a curated, on-topic corpus instead of relying on any single textbook.
evidence: Europe PMC REST: query=* -> 48,938,549; IN_PMC:Y -> 12,296,246; OPEN_ACCESS:Y -> 8,273,746; OPEN_ACCESS:Y AND LICENSE:"CC BY" -> 5,305,272; OPEN_ACCESS:Y AND LICENSE:"CC BY NC" -> 1,010,123; NCBI E-utilities db=pmc 'neurotoxicity' -> 258,530; 'curcumin neuroprotection' -> 27,685
license: Per-article OA license - CC BY (~5.3M) is commercially redistributable (shippable); CC BY-NC (~1.0M) is non-commercial (reference-only); NC/other must be filtered out
fit_small_data: medium - the full corpus is too big to ship; the value is the LICENSE-filtered, topic-curated subset (tens of thousands of records)
fit_onnx_cpu: high - the pipeline is CPU (download, license-filter, chunk, embed, index); no GPU
risk: License is per-article, not corpus-level: a bulk dump mixes CC BY and CC BY-ND/other, so per-record license gating is mandatory or the app risks shipping non-redistributable text

name: AOP-Wiki (Adverse Outcome Pathway corpus) - neurotoxicity AOPs & key events
what: The collaborative AOP corpus: 598 AOPs, 1,947 key events, 3,185 key-event relationships, 874 prototypical stressors (release 2.8, 2026), downloadable as quarterly + nightly XML plus flat TSV (KE/KER) files - including neurotoxicity pathways (mitochondrial complex I, oxidative stress, NMDA/neurodegeneration, AChE inhibition, neurite/neurodevelopment).
why_better: Old plan's 'post-hoc bio prior' was an unstructured black box; the AOP-Wiki gives a small, structured, CC BY-SA mechanistic graph (MIE -> KE -> adverse outcome) the app can retrieve to explain the causal chain behind each NTI sub-score - a far stronger, citable, offline 'bio prior' than a hand-tuned one.
evidence: AOP-Wiki metrics page: AOPs 598, Key events 1,947, KE relationships 3,185, Prototypical Stressors 874, author-users 402; nightly XML ~49.5 MB; TSV KE/KER files confirm structure (e.g. AOP 3 mitochondrial complex I -> Parkinsonian motor deficits; AOP 17 oxidative-stress neurotoxicity)
license: CC BY-SA (default since release 2.6, 2023; some AOPs time-limited All-Rights-Reserved then auto-convert to BY-SA) - shippable with attribution/share-alike on the content
fit_small_data: high - ~598 AOPs / 1,947 KEs is tiny and fully curable; directly mechanistic for neurotoxicity
fit_onnx_cpu: high - parse XML/TSV to a small graph + embeddings; CPU only
risk: BY-SA is viral for derived content - bundling requires attribution and share-alike on the AOP text; ARR-licensed AOPs must be filtered to their license expiry

name: LibreTexts - Medicine / Neuroscience (open-access textbook library)
what: The multi-institutional LibreTexts open textbook library; the Medicine/Health-Sciences library (med.libretexts.org) hosts freely-editable neuroscience and toxicology texts with stable page IDs - a modern, living alternative to the 1999/2001 Bookshelf editions.
why_better: Old plan's static textbook grounding was dated (1999/2001); LibreTexts provides up-to-date, page-ID-citable open content that can be re-crawled, so the offline corpus can be refreshed without repurchasing a book.
evidence: med.libretexts.org Health Sciences library loaded and confirmed live (part of LibreTexts); per-page CC license and exact neuroscience-book record count not confirmed in-session (unverified)
license: CC BY-NC-SA (standard LibreTexts license; per-page license unverified in-session) -> non-commercial: conditional for a commercial offline app, reference/extract only unless page-level license confirmed
fit_small_data: high - modular open pages, easy to chunk by page ID
fit_onnx_cpu: high - static text; CPU retrieval only
risk: Standard LibreTexts license is non-commercial (NC-SA); verify each page's license before bundling, otherwise treat as reference-only

name: (design) License-gated offline RAG packaging via Europe PMC LICENSE: facets
what: A build-time packaging pipeline that queries Europe PMC with LICENSE:"CC BY" / "CC BY NC" facets to split the OA pool into a commercially-redistributable shard (bundle into the app) and a non-commercial shard (reference/link only), stamping each chunk with source, PMCID/DOI and exact CC code.
why_better: Old plan had no legal-safety mechanism for an offline corpus; gating on the LICENSE: field (verified: CC BY 5,305,272 vs CC BY NC 1,010,123) is the single control that converts 'open access' into 'legally shippable', preventing the most likely offline-app liability (bundling NC/ND text).
evidence: Verified in-session: Europe PMC REST OPEN_ACCESS:Y AND LICENSE:"CC BY" = 5,305,272; OPEN_ACCESS:Y AND LICENSE:"CC BY NC" = 1,010,123 - the two shards are cleanly separable at query time
fit_small_data: high - one build script; works on any corpus size; the shippable shard stays small after topic curation
risk: LICENSE: facet is Europe-PMC's inferred value, not a legal guarantee; keep a per-record license field and re-check high-stakes records; NC-ND and other licenses must be excluded, not just NC

name: (design) Section/chapter-anchored chunking + structured metadata schema
what: Chunk by document structure, not fixed tokens: Bookshelf chapter/section (NBK ids), AOP-Wiki AOP->KE, OECD section, PMC article->section. Every chunk carries structured metadata (source, license, PMCID/DOI/NBK, chapter, year, organism/cell-line: PC12/SH-SY5Y, toxin: H2O2/DOX/curcumin, NTI sub-score link) for filtered retrieval and citations.
why_better: Old plan's SHAP-only XAI explains the model, not the biology; structure-anchored chunks with toxin/cell-line metadata let the RAG return short, correctly-scoped, citation-bearing passages (e.g. 'curcumin + PC12 + neurite') so explanations are grounded AND auditable, which plain token chunks cannot do.
evidence: Structure available in-session: Bookshelf chapter-level records (nbk ids), AOP-Wiki AOP/KE/KER TSV with confidence columns (High/Moderate/Low), Europe PMC resultType=core full text - all expose natural section boundaries
fit_small_data: high - deterministic, no training; metadata is cheap to extract from the structured sources above
fit_onnx_cpu: high - CPU tokenization/embedding + SQLite/FAISS index; no GPU
risk: Over-chunking dilutes citations; under-chunking splits a mechanism across chunks - needs a section-aware splitter and a citation-per-chunk invariant

name: (design) AOP-Wiki KE/KER graph index for mechanistic retrieval
what: Parse the AOP-Wiki TSV/XML (AOP, key events, key-event relationships with High/Moderate/Low confidence) into a small offline graph; at query time, map an observed NTI sub-score (e.g. reduced neurite length) to candidate MIE->KE->adverse-outcome chains and retrieve the supporting AOP text as the explanation.
why_better: Old plan's bio prior produced a number with no causal story; a KE/KER graph turns each NTI sub-score into a retrievable causal chain with per-link confidence, giving offline, evidence-graded mechanistic explanations (e.g. H2O2 -> ROS -> oxidative stress -> neurodegeneration) that a flat corpus cannot.
evidence: Verified structure in-session: aop_ke_ker.tsv rows = Aop / upstream Event / downstream Event / Relationship / adjacent|non-adjacent / confidence (1-High,2-Moderate,3-Low,5-NS); 3,185 KERs and 598 AOPs from metrics page
license: n/a - design pattern (builds on the CC BY-SA AOP-Wiki content above)
fit_small_data: high - ~598 nodes/3,185 edges is a trivial CPU graph; no training
fit_onnx_cpu: high - in-memory graph + small embeddings; CPU only
risk: AOP coverage of PC12/H2O2/DOX/curcumin specifically is sparse - most neuro AOPs are for other stressors; treat chains as hypothesis-generating, and carry the confidence grade into the explanation
